RWA 3 $2.2T Cash and marketable securities 4 $1.5T Average loans $1.6T Firmwide Metrics n Reported revenue of $50.2 billion and managed revenue 2 of $50.9 billion n Expense of $27.3 billion; reported overhead ratio of 54% and managed overhead ratio 2 of 54% n Credit costs of $2.7 billion with $2.2 billion of net charge-offs and a $539 million net reserve build n Average loans up 10% YoY and 2% QoQ; average deposits up 8% YoY and 2% QoQ CCB ROE 36% n Average deposits up 4% YoY, flat QoQ; client investment assets up 15% YoY n Average loans up 2% YoY and 1% QoQ; Card Services net charge-off rate of 2.91% n Debit and credit card sales volume 5 up 10% YoY n Active mobile customers 6 up 7% YoY CIB ROE 18% n Investment Banking fees up 14% YoY, down 8% QoQ; #1 ranking for Global Investment Banking fees with 9.2% wallet share YTD 7 n Markets revenue up 15% YoY, with Fixed Income Markets down 4% and Equity Markets up 49% n Average Banking & Payments loans up 11% YoY, flat QoQ; average client deposits 8 up 10% YoY, up 1% QoQ AWM ROE 45% n AUM 9 of $5.2 trillion, up 13% YoY n Average loans up 20% YoY and 6% QoQ; average deposits up 5% YoY, down 3% QoQ Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, commented on the financial results: “The Firm reported another quarter of strong results, generating net income of $15.8 billion and an ROTCE of 21%, excluding discretionary investment securities losses totaling $498 million after tax.” Dimon continued: “Each line of business performed well. In the CIB, revenue increased 14%. Markets revenue and IB fees each rose at a mid-teens rate, helped by strong levels of client activity, although activity did moderate somewhat during the quarter. Meanwhile, Payments and Securities Services each posted double-digit revenue increases led by ongoing deposit and fee growth. In CCB, revenue rose 9%. We ranked #1 in U.S. retail deposits for the sixth consecutive year, and account acquisition remained strong in the quarter as we added over 650,000 net new checking accounts. Additionally, growth continued to be robust in Card, with strong demand for our set of products. Finally, in AWM, revenue grew 14%, and flows were very strong with $263 billion of client asset net inflows.” Dimon added: “Our capital hierarchy has remained consistent over time, with investing in the franchise and supporting our clients at the top. In line with our hierarchy, we reduced share repurchases this quarter. We believe we can deploy this capital over time at very attractive returns for our shareholders.” Dimon added: “The U.S. economy continued to be fueled by strong business investment and ongoing consumer spending. However, large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates and geopolitical conditions continue to shift under the surface. These forces may be manageable, but we remain prepared for a wide range of outcomes.” Dimon concluded: “I want to express my deep gratitude to our employees across the globe for how they work to support our customers and communities every single day.” SIGNIFICANT ITEM IN 3Q26 RESULTS n $658 million of net investment securities losses in Corporate 10 ($0.18 decrease in EPS 11 ) CAPITAL DISTRIBUTIONS n Common dividend of $4.4 billion or $1.65 per share n $664 million of common stock net repurchases 12 n Net payout LTM 12,13 of 61% FORTRESS PRINCIPLES n Book value per share of $132.30, up 6% YoY; tangible book value per share 2 of $112.64, up 7% YoY n Basel III common equity Tier 1 capital 3 of $304 billion, Standardized ratio 3 of 13.9% and Advanced ratio 3 of 14.1% n Firm supplementary leverage ratio of 5.5% SUPPORTED CONSUMERS, BUSINESSES & COMMUNITIES n Approximately $2.9 trillion of credit and capital 14 raised YTD: n $240 billion of credit for consumers n $27 billion of credit for U.S. small businesses n $2.5 trillion of credit and capital for corporations 15 and non-U.S. government entities n $79 billion of credit and capital for nonprofit and U.S. government entities, including states, municipalities, hospitals and universities Investor Contact: Mikael Grubb (212) 270-2479 Media Contact: Joseph Evangelisti (212) 270-7438 Note: Totals may not sum due to rounding. 1 Percentage comparisons are for the third quarter of 2026 versus the prior-year third quarter, unless otherwise specified. 2 For notes on non-GAAP financial measures, including managed basis reporting, see page 6. Net revenue was $50.9 billion, up 8%. Net interest income was $27.1 billion, up 13%. Noninterest revenue was $23.8 billion, up 3%. Net interest income excluding Markets 2 was $24.7 billion, up 6%, driven by higher deposit balances, higher balances in Card Services and higher wholesale loan balances, partially offset by the impact of lower rates. Noninterest revenue excluding Markets 2 was $15.9 billion, up 7%, or up 12% also excluding $658 million of net investment securities losses, driven by higher asset management fees in AWM and CCB, higher investment banking fees, higher card income and higher auto operating lease income, partially offset by net losses on certain equity investments. Markets revenue was $10.3 billion, up 15%, predominantly driven by higher Equity Markets revenue. The provision for credit losses was $2.7 billion. Net charge-offs were $2.2 billion, down $389 million, driven by Wholesale. The net reserve build was $539 million, primarily in Wholesale. Investment Banking fees were $3.0 billion, up 14%, predominantly driven by higher advisory fees. Payments revenue was $5.6 billion, up 14%, driven by higher deposit balances, higher deposit margin and fee growth. Lending revenue was $2.2 billion, up 20%, largely driven by lower losses on hedges of the retained lending portfolio and higher loan balances. reference.summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. operates as a bank and financial holding company in the United States, rest of North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Caribbean. It operates in three segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. The company offers deposit, investment and lending products, and cash management; mortgage origination and servicing activities; residential mortgages and home equity loans; and credit cards, payment solutions, travel services, merchant offers, lifestyle benefits, auto loans, and leases to consumers and small businesses through bank branches, ATMs, and digital and telephone banking. It also provides investment banking, market-making, financing, custody, and securities products and services; corporate strategy and structure advisory, equity and debt market capital-raising,
